extra.message: User-controlled 'filter' GraphQL argument is interpolated via %-formatting directly into a raw SQL string passed to sqlalchemy.text() in resolve_pastes. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. filter="' OR 1=1--") to dump or manipulate the database.

resolve_system_debug concatenates the unauthenticated user-controlled 'arg' argument into 'ps {}' and passes it to helpers.run_cmd() which calls os.popen(). This allows unauthenticated remote OS command injection (e.g. arg='; id').

ImportPaste.mutate builds a shell command 'curl --insecure <url>' from user-controlled scheme/host/port/path and executes it via helpers.run_cmd() (os.popen). security.strip_dangerous_characters() returns input unchanged in easy mode and only strips ';' and '&' in hard mode, leaving $( ), backticks, |, newlines etc., allowing remote command injection.

resolve_system_diagnostics executes the user-supplied 'cmd' argument via helpers.run_cmd() (os.popen) after a weak credential check. security.allowed_cmds() returns True unconditionally in easy mode, granting arbitrary OS command execution; even in hard mode startswith(('echo','ps' 'whoami','tail')) is trivially bypassable (note the missing comma creating 'pswhoami').

ImportPaste.mutate lets an unauthenticated user specify arbitrary scheme, host, port, and path, which are used to fetch a URL with 'curl --insecure'. This is a server-side request forgery allowing scanning/attacking internal network services; --insecure also disables TLS certificate verification.

save_file() concatenates the user-controlled 'filename' argument (from the UploadPaste GraphQL mutation, core/views.py:186) directly onto WEB_UPLOADDIR and opens it for writing with no sanitization. A filename like '../../app.py' allows arbitrary file write/overwrite on the server (path traversal).

get_identity() decodes JWT tokens with verify_signature=False and verify_exp=False. Any attacker can forge a token with identity='admin' and pass it to the 'me' query (core/views.py:283), which then exposes real user passwords via UserObject.resolve_password (core/views.py:62). This is a complete authentication bypass.

Flask SECRET_KEY and JWT_SECRET_KEY are hardcoded to the literal string 'dvga'. Anyone with source access can forge valid JWT access/refresh tokens and Flask session cookies, bypassing authentication.

Database seeding creates the 'admin' account with password chosen from a list containing only 'changeme' (line 49) and 'operator' with hardcoded password 'password123'. These predictable default credentials allow trivial login via the Login mutation.

User passwords are stored in plaintext (no hashing) and compared in plaintext in the Login mutation (core/views.py:234: filter_by(username=username, password=password)). Any database read (e.g. via the SQL injection in resolve_pastes) discloses all credentials.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: EditPaste.mutate performs no authentication or ownership check; any unauthenticated user can modify the title/content of any paste by id (IDOR / broken object-level authorization).
DeletePaste.mutate has no authentication or ownership verification; any unauthenticated user can delete arbitrary pastes by id (IDOR).

resolve_delete_all_pastes exposes an unauthenticated GraphQL field that deletes every row in the pastes table (Paste.query.delete()) with no authorization check, allowing anonymous mass data destruction.
resolve_read_and_burn lets any unauthenticated user read and delete private 'burn after reading' pastes by id, with no ownership or authorization check (IDOR on sensitive objects).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: resolve_users and resolve_audits expose the full user list and complete GraphQL audit log (containing operation names and queries) to unauthenticated clients with no access control, enabling information disclosure and user enumeration.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: UserObject.resolve_password returns the real plaintext password whenever info.context.json['identity'] == 'admin', and that identity value is set from a JWT whose signature is never verified (core/helpers.py:21). Any client can therefore retrieve all user passwords via GraphQL.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: format_custom_error() embeds full Python stack traces (traceback.format_stack/format_exc) and absolute internal file paths into GraphQL error responses returned to clients, disclosing sensitive internal implementation details useful for further attacks.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: sys.setrecursionlimit(100000) raises the recursion limit to an extreme value, enabling deeply nested GraphQL queries (especially in easy mode where the depth middleware is bypassed) to cause stack exhaustion / denial of service.

simulate_load() (invoked by the unauthenticated system_update query, core/views.py:333) sleeps in a loop up to ~50 seconds per request with no rate limiting; repeated calls tie up workers and cause denial of service.

The /graphql endpoint is registered without restricting HTTP methods and the view processes GET requests (OverriddenView.dispatch_request handles 'get'), and no CSRF protection exists anywhere in the app. State-changing mutations can be triggered cross-site via simple GET requests (CSRF).

resp.set_cookie('env', 'graphiql:disable') sets a security-relevant cookie (used by IGQLProtectionMiddleware to gate GraphiQL access) without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes, and its value is fully client-controllable so the protection is trivially bypassed.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The /graphql endpoint enables batch=True with no per-batch limit and, in default (easy) mode, all protective middlewares (depth, cost, introspection, denylist) short-circuit, leaving introspection enabled and allowing batch/alias-based brute-force and abuse of the Login mutation with no rate limiting.
